name: MAKE THE BELIEF BET
title: MAKE THE BELIEF BET
mechanism: State Belief → Picture Outcome → Pay Out
goal: Test a belief with a small action that could prove it wrong — aim current charge.
steps:
1. State the belief as a clear prediction.
2. Choose a safe, small action that could prove it wrong as well as right.
3. Picture the expected result before acting.
4. Run the test, then compare observation with prediction.
5. Pay out only to evidence.

name: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
title: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
mechanism: Name → Remain Version → Climb Stair
goal: Start at the smallest task level that still leaves real evidence; channel useful momentum.
steps:
1. Name five versions of the task from almost easy to genuinely stretching.
2. Mentally remove the zero-effort decoy.
3. Do the smallest remaining version that leaves visible evidence—one paragraph, one call, one plate washed.
4. Next time, climb only one stair.

name: MOOD HAS ALIBIS
title: MOOD HAS ALIBIS
mechanism: Choose Activity → Add Sentence → Try Three Ways
goal: Redirect useful drive: compare predicted mood with what actually changes during real activities.
steps:
1. Choose one activity.
2. Before it, score expected mood; at the start, notice your actual mood; at the end, score again.
3. Add one sentence about what changed during the activity.
4. Repeat with three different actions before deciding ‘nothing helps.’

name: TWO ENGINES
title: TWO ENGINES
mechanism: Schedule Chosen → Check Both → Drop Demand
goal: Feed pleasure and mastery separately instead of asking one activity to fix everything — steady useful momentum.
steps:
1. For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence.
2. Make both small enough to happen.
3. After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only.
4. Do not demand that either activity fix everything.

name: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
title: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
mechanism: Pick Desired → Add Deliberate → Let Space Vote
goal: Guide rising drive; make the wanted behaviour easier to enter and the unwanted default harder to reach.
steps:
1. Pick one desired behaviour and one unwanted default.
2. Picture the desired route becoming easier and the unwanted route becoming slightly harder.
3. Imagine one extra decision appearing before the unwanted default can happen.
4. Mentally rehearse taking the easier desired route once.

name: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
title: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
mechanism: Name Cue → Keep Hands → Let Learning Land
goal: Let an urge rise and fall without doing the usual ritual; channel high charge.
steps:

5. Choose what protects the next hour.

name: COOL THE ALARM PANEL
title: COOL THE ALARM PANEL
mechanism: Use Cool → Remove Name → End the Cool
goal: Pace current energy; use brief comfortable coolness as a reset cue, not a toughness test.
steps:
1. Use cool—not painfully cold—water or a wrapped cool pack on the cheeks and around the eyes for a brief interval.
2. Slow your body while the sensation lands.
3. Remove it, name the room, and reassess the next safe action.
4. Treat the cool sensation as a reset cue. Stop before it becomes an endurance test.

name: THE LONGER OUT-BREATH
title: THE LONGER OUT-BREATH
mechanism: Breathe Pulling → Repeat Comfortable → Breathe Workable
goal: Harness rising charge: lengthen the out-breath gently, then make one workable decision from a steadier pace.
steps:
1. Breathe in without pulling extra air.
2. Let the outflow last slightly longer, as though fogging a distant window silently.
3. Repeat only while comfortable; keep shoulders quiet and jaw loose.
4. After several rounds, resume natural breathing and look for one workable decision.

3. Name the mismatch before leaving.
4. Repeat later under safe conditions rather than chasing maximum distress.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Stay with a manageable fear cue long enough to notice reality contradict one prediction — guide high charge.

STEPS
1. Choose an external cue low enough on your fear ladder to approach voluntarily.
2. Enter without escape and remain until you observe at least one mismatch between prediction and reality.
3. Name the mismatch before leaving.
4. Repeat later under safe conditions rather than chasing maximum distress.

WIN
You left after naming one mismatch between what you expected and what actually occurred.

RETURN KEY
Pressure surges · STAYUPDATE
Enter Escape · STAYUPDATE
STAYUPDATE · Repeat Later

MIND BEND
Fear updates from discrepancy, not from endurance. The useful moment is when prediction and reality stop matching.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose External → Enter Escape → Name Mismatch → Repeat Later

SAFETY
PAUSE
Exposure needs clinical support when trauma, medical risk, severe phobia, or feeling unreal or disconnected is involved.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

name: DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT
title: DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT
mechanism: Trauma time collapse family: name today's date opens a route toward return to room.
goal: Anchor to today's date using the room, an exit, and reachable support — harness extra rush.
steps:
1. Say today's full date and your current location aloud.
2. Read the names of three ordinary objects directly in front of you.
3. Point to the nearest low-risk exit without moving toward the past memory.
4. Name one person or service available in the present.
5. Keep eyes open and return attention to the whole room.

name: FEAR WITHOUT THE MOVIE
title: FEAR WITHOUT THE MOVIE
mechanism: Locate Most → Keep Hand → Let Raw
goal: Feel fear as raw body sensation without letting prediction turn it into a movie — slow hot rush.
steps:
1. If safely steady, locate the most intense fear sensation and say only its movement, charge, heat, and boundary.
2. Remove prediction briefly.

name: MOVE THE CHARGE INTO A CONTAINER
title: MOVE THE CHARGE INTO A CONTAINER
mechanism: Choose Shaking → Keep Movement → Take Earliest Move
goal: Convert current surge: move anger or alarm through controlled physical effort without rehearsing harm.
steps:
1. Choose shaking, wall-free pushing motions, stamping, stretching, or strong walking.
2. Decide a safe maximum intensity and ten controlled repetitions.

title: WIDEN THE PRESENT CAMERA
mechanism: Near-Far Visual Sweep → Widen Room → Name Place → Choose Action

name: ASK WHAT THE MEMORY IS STILL BILLING
title: ASK WHAT THE MEMORY IS STILL BILLING
mechanism: Headline Event → Route Bill → Act Present
goal: Find what a memory is still demanding and route that demand to the right present response; find useful traction.
steps:
1. State the event as one factual headline with no motive and without rebuilding sensory details.
2. Finish this sentence once: ‘This memory still seems to demand ___.’ Keep only one claim.
3. Route the claim to BOUNDARY, REPAIR, GRIEF, or IMPOSSIBLE REVERSAL. Do not create a fifth category.
4. Choose the matching present response: set protection, request safe repair, make room for grief, or stop billing today for a reversal history cannot provide.

name: THE LAST 5% TAX
title: THE LAST 5% TAX
challenge: You are waiting for perfect closure
moment: You are waiting for perfect closure
mechanism: Find Polish Loop → Set Enough Line → Close Once
goal: Stop paying for a perfect ending when a clean enough ending already protects what matters; redirect high charge.
steps:
1. Name the last detail you keep polishing, checking, or waiting to feel settled about.
2. Ask what real harm would happen if you stopped now. Ignore discomfort that is not actual harm.
3. Set one ‘enough’ line: accurate enough, kind enough, complete enough, or safe enough.
4. Take one closing action—send, save, archive, leave, or stop.
5. Do not reopen it unless new information appears.

name: LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN
title: LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN
challenge: You are trying to suppress an intrusive thought
moment: You are trying to suppress an intrusive thought
mechanism: Permission + attention redirection reduce suppression rebound by ending the fight to force an intrusive thought out of awareness.
goal: Stop fighting the thought and continue one small task without checking whether it left — channel sharp surge.
steps:
1. Say, “This thought is allowed to be here for this minute.”
2. Notice one sound or object outside your head without turning it into an escape or proof.
3. Start one small task while letting the thought remain in the background.
4. Do not check whether the thought has faded before continuing.
